html:
Tenochtitlan was the capital of the Mexica, or Aztecs, a city on an island in Lake Texcoco in the Valley of Mexico. It was founded around 1325 and destroyed by the Spanish in 1521. Mexico City stands on its ruins.

The Mexica built it out into the lake with chinampas, raised garden plots, and joined it to the shore with causeways. An aqueduct brought fresh water from Chapultepec. By 1519 it may have had 200,000 people or more, though estimates vary, which put it among the largest cities in the world. At its centre stood the walled sacred precinct with the Templo Mayor, the twin temple of Huitzilopochtli and Tlaloc. Its twin city Tlatelolco held the great market, where the pochteca traded goods from across Mesoamerica.

From 1428 it led the Triple Alliance with Texcoco and Tlacopan, and tribute flowed in from a large empire. Hernán Cortés entered in 1519 as a guest of Moctezuma II. A revolt drove the Spanish out in 1520, then smallpox struck the city. In 1521 a long siege, fought with tens of thousands of Indigenous allies, ended in the fall of Tenochtitlan. The Spanish built their capital over it, and the cathedral stands beside the old temple.
sum: Tenochtitlan was the capital of the Mexica, or Aztecs, a city on an island in Lake Texcoco in the Valley of Mexico. It was founded around 1325 and destroyed by the Spanish in 1521. Mexico City stands on its ruins.
